slides.text:
The last module filled holes with values. Now the template decides: it shows parts only when a condition holds, repeats parts for every item, and calls functions.

You will use `if`, `range` and `with`, then variables, pipelines, the built-in functions and your own.
The data is still maps and slices. Everything runs on `text/template`: text with actions between `{{` and `}}`.

`{{if}}` shows a part only when its condition is true, and `{{else}}` covers the rest. Every block closes with `{{end}}`.

The snippet is pseudo code.
A value is false when it is empty: `false`, `0`, an empty string, an empty slice or map, or `nil`. Any other value is true.
Comparisons are functions, and the function name comes first: `eq`, `ne`, `lt`, `le`, `gt` and `ge`. Both values must be the same kind, numbers with numbers or text with text.
`and`, `or` and `not` are functions too, so the name comes first. Put a call inside parentheses to use its result as an argument.

slides.text:
`{{range}}` repeats its part for each item of a slice, and inside it the dot is the current item. Its `{{else}}` runs when there are no items.

The snippet is pseudo code.
`{{with value}}` is an `if` that also moves the dot. If the value is not empty, the dot becomes that value inside the block. Its `{{else}}` runs otherwise.
Inside a loop, `{{break}}` leaves it and `{{continue}}` goes to the next item.

slides.text:
A variable keeps a value: `{{$name := value}}`. Inside `range` and `with` the dot changes, but a variable keeps what it held.

The snippet is pseudo code.
`range` can name what it loops with: `{{range $i, $v := .}}` gives the position and the item of a slice, or the key and the value of a map. Map keys come in sorted order.
A few functions are built in: `len` counts, `index` takes an item by position or key, and `printf` formats like `fmt.Sprintf`. Call them with the arguments after the name.
A pipeline sends a value through functions with `|`. The value on the left becomes the **last** argument of the function on the right, so the two lines below are the same.

You can add your own functions. Give each a name in a `FuncMap`, and attach the map with `Funcs` **before** `Parse`, because parsing checks that every function exists.

A function returns one value, or a value and an error. The snippet is pseudo code.
